newsitem.title: USA: Longshoremen buy Conn.'s two busiest ports - paper.
newsitem.headline: Longshoremen buy Conn.'s two busiest ports - paper.

text.p: A local Longshoremen's union, trying to save the jobs of its members, has purchased two of Connecticut's busiest ports, New Haven and Bridgeport, the Hartford Courant said in its Friday edition.

An official with the Connecticut Development Authority told the paper that the New Haven port handles around 500,000 tons of mostly metal and paper products every year, while Bridgeport handles about 175,000 tons. The official was not immediately available to comment.

The new company, Coastline Terminals of Connecticut Inc, which now owns about 70 percent of the terminals, is led by David Shuda, a union official and president. The Connecticut Development Authority is backing 35 percent of a $10 million bank loan for the project, the paper said.

The state, which hopes to save about 250 jobs at the terminals and 1,000 more related positions, also hopes that the ports could develop into tourist attractions. But the paper said recent studies have shown that the potential return on investments in ports is uncertain.
